newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-BJORN'S RYDER CUP HOPES THREATENED BY INJURY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BJORN'S RYDER CUP HOPES THREATENED BY INJURY.

text.p: Denmark's Thomas Bjorn pulled out of the Scandinavian Masters on Tuesday after a jogging accident which could threaten his Ryder Cup prospects.
The 26-year-old Dane, currently seventh in the Ryder Cup table, sprained his ankle while running at the weekend and his doctor told him to rest the foot for at least a week.
Europe's 1996 rookie of the year, Bjorn became the first Dane to win a European Tour event when he took last year's World Invitational.

A spokesman for Bjorn's management said: "A doctor advised him to rest so that he will be fully fit to play the following week's Czech Open and then go on to take up his invitation to the U.S. PGA Championship.
While he may be out for only a week, missing the Scandinavian Masters is a blow to Bjorn.
Last year he led the event briefly when it was staged in Gothenburg before finishing seventh and he fancied his chances of improving on that.

With most of his rivals for a place in the European Ryder Cup team playing in Malmo this week, Bjorn will look to consolidate his position in the remaining four events to count for automatic top 10 qualifying places.
